title.root: Rubik's Cube Solver: 2x2–15x15, Pyraminx, Skewb, Megaminx
desc.root: Free online Rubik's Cube solver for 2x2–15x15 cubes, Pyraminx, Skewb and Megaminx. Paint or scan your puzzle and follow the solution step by step in 3D.
intro.root: {site} solves Rubik's Cubes from 2×2 to 15×15, the Pyraminx, the Skewb and the Megaminx directly in your browser. Enter your scrambled puzzle by painting a net, scanning it with your camera or typing the scramble, press Solve and follow the solution on an animated 3D model. A permutation graph shows how every sticker travels along its orbit.

howto.title: How to solve a {name} with this solver
howto.s1: Hold your {name} the way the net shows (this page already selects the {name}).
howto.s1Root: Choose your puzzle in the menu at the top: 2×2 to 15×15, Pyraminx, Skewb or Megaminx.
howto.s2cube: Enter the scrambled state: paint the stickers on the net, scan every face with your camera or upload photos, or type the scramble in standard notation.
howto.s2twisty: Enter the scrambled state: paint the stickers on the net or type the scramble in notation.
howto.s3: Press Solve. The solver runs inside your browser; nothing is uploaded.
howto.s4: Follow the solution: the 3D model turns step by step while the permutation graph shows every sticker moving. In Free play mode you can scramble and turn the puzzle yourself, with a timer.
solver.title: Solver and measured move counts
solver.cube2: Proven optimal: a complete distance table of all 3,674,160 positions is built in about 0.3 s. In {samples} random scrambles the solutions had {avg} moves on average and at most {max} (half-turn metric).
solver.cube3: Kociemba's two-phase algorithm (cubejs) with iterative shortening; positions within 8 moves of solved are solved optimally. Solutions are usually {range} moves (half-turn metric) and appear in about a second.
solver.cube4: Our own reduction solver: first the centers, then edge pairing with OLL and PLL parity fixed, then the 3×3 stage. In {samples} random scrambles the solutions had {avg} moves on average (outer block turn metric) and took about {sec} s. gullicube can be selected as an alternative.
solver.big: gullicube by Tomas Rokicki, compiled to multithreaded WebAssembly. In our tests a random {n}×{n} scramble took about {q} moves in quality mode (10–15 s, about 30 MB of tables downloaded once) or about {f} moves in fast mode (2–4 s), counted in the single slice turn metric.
solver.pyraminx: Proven optimal: a complete breadth-first table of all 933,120 positions (without tips) is built in about a quarter of a second. Every position needs at most {coreMax} turns plus up to {tipsMax} tip turns; random positions need {avg} moves on average including tips.
solver.skewb: Proven optimal: a complete breadth-first table of all 3,149,280 positions is built in under half a second. No position needs more than {max} moves; random positions need {avg} moves on average.
notation.title: Notation
notation.cube: Standard WCA notation: U D L R F B turn a face clockwise, ' means counterclockwise and 2 a half turn; x y z rotate the whole cube.
notation.mid: M E S turn the middle slice.
notation.big: On bigger cubes a number in front selects an inner layer (2R) and w turns several layers together (Rw, 3Rw).
notation.pyraminx: U L R B turn the two layers at the top, left, right or back vertex by 120°; lowercase u l r b turn only the tip; ' means counterclockwise.
notation.skewb: WCA Skewb notation (white on top, green in front): R U L B turn the half of the puzzle around that corner by 120°; ' means counterclockwise. The top-front-right corner never moves.
graph.title: What the permutation graph shows
graph.cube: Every sticker is a node. Each move permutes the stickers and splits them into cycles, drawn as circles: on a {n}×{n} cube the {n} layers of each of the three axes appear as {n} concentric circles. A solution is a path through the puzzle's state graph from your scramble to the solved state, and the graph animates that path move by move.
graph.twisty: Every sticker is a node. Each 120° turn moves stickers in 3-cycles, drawn as circles, so you can see exactly which pieces a move touches. A solution is a path through the puzzle's state graph from your scramble to the solved state, and the graph animates that path move by move.
graph.root: Every sticker is a node and every move is a permutation of the stickers. The permutation splits into cycles, drawn as circles, so the graph shows the structure of the puzzle: which stickers can reach which places. A solution is a path through the puzzle's state graph from your scramble to the solved state, and the graph animates that path move by move.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.free.q: Is the solver free, and are my photos uploaded?
faq.free.a: It is free and runs entirely in your browser. Camera images and photos are processed on your device and never uploaded. The site counts visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which uses no cookies; Google Analytics is loaded only if you accept it in the banner, and you can change that choice in the footer.
faq.optimal.q: Is the solution the shortest possible?
faq.optimal.yes: Yes. The solver uses a complete table of every position, so each solution has the fewest possible moves.
faq.optimal.cube3: Positions within 8 moves of solved are solved optimally; otherwise the two-phase solver returns a near-optimal solution, usually {range} moves.
faq.optimal.cube4: No. The reduction method gives about {avg} moves; finding optimal 4×4 solutions is far beyond what a browser can do.
faq.optimal.big: No. Optimal solving of a {n}×{n} cube is out of reach for any computer; gullicube is one of the strongest practical solvers and is about {q} moves here.
faq.optimal.root: 2×2, Pyraminx and Skewb solutions are proven optimal. 3×3 solutions are near-optimal (usually 19–21 moves). From 4×4 up the solvers use reduction methods, so solutions are longer but are found in seconds.
faq.scan.q: Can I scan my {name} with the camera?
faq.scan.qRoot: Can I scan my cube with the camera?
faq.scan.cube: Yes. Open the Camera / photo tab, show each face to the camera or upload a photo of each face, then check the result on the net and correct any sticker before solving.
faq.scan.twisty: Not yet: camera scanning is available for 2×2 to 15×15 cubes. Paint the stickers on the net (it takes about a minute) or type the scramble in notation.
faq.scan.root: Yes, for cubes from 2×2 to 15×15: show each face to the camera or upload photos, then check the colors on the net. The Pyraminx, Skewb and Megaminx are entered by painting.
faq.puzzles.a: Cubes from 2×2 to 15×15, the Pyraminx, the Skewb and the Megaminx. Each one has its own page with notation and measured move counts.

desc.megaminx: Free Megaminx solver: paint the 12 faces or type a WCA scramble, press Solve and follow a complete solution (about {avg} moves) on a 3D model.
intro.megaminx: Solve any Megaminx in your browser: paint the colors on the two-flower net or type the scramble, press Solve and follow the solution face by face on a 3D model.
solver.megaminx: A fast multi-phase solver running in a Web Worker: it builds the puzzle face by face with small search tables and finishes the last layer with a two-look table of generated algorithms. On {samples} random positions it needed {avg} moves on average (at most {max}, WCA-style HTM: every 72° or 144° face turn counts 1) in about {ms} ms. The solutions are not optimal.
notation.megaminx: Face turns (white on top, green in front): U F R L BL BR for the top and upper faces, D FL FR DL DR B for the bottom and lower faces. No suffix is 72° clockwise, ' counterclockwise, 2 is 144°. WCA Pochmann scrambles (R++ R-- D++ D-- U U') are accepted too.
graph.megaminx: Every one of the 132 stickers is a node. The stickers are placed by a stereographic projection of the dodecahedron from the bottom center, so every face turn moves stickers in 5-cycles along true circles: the upper faces give rings around the middle, the lower faces five big petals. The graph animates the solution move by move.
faq.optimal.megaminx: No. Optimal Megaminx solving is far out of reach; this solver is built for speed and returns a complete solution of about {avg} moves in a fraction of a second.
